_doc: Observations about agent/model reliability. Advisory: the current user directive pins ALL agents to Opus 4.8 at max effort (see agent frontmatter). These notes record observed wedge patterns so the orchestrator's anti-wedge handling (firm kill+respawn) knows where to be vigilant. NOT a model override — the directive is Opus everywhere.

observations.observation: Observed planner wedging (zero writes / zero heartbeats for 8+ min, repeated across two attempts) in an earlier configuration. Under the current Opus-max directive (all agents run Opus at max effort), treat any planner silence past the dead-agent threshold as a wedge and invoke the dead-planner fallback (assumed fills) + ONE firm respawn — do NOT wait out two full stage windows.

Builders wedge most often on the comment-thread/comment-dialog family (the known-hard block). Combine with component-difficulty: build that family MINIMAL and enforce the firm kill+respawn on a heartbeat-silence past the hard budget so one wedged builder can't stall the whole run.

Plans a correct compose tree and reasons well about SDK internals, but will anchor R2 context on a container-shaped tag that is not a registered element. Gate every planned primitive on registered:true.

A drive that OPENS a surface is not a drive that reaches a STATE. Six card-state blocks all captured the first (single-comment) thread and every gate stayed green. Scope liveSelector to the instance that exhibits the state (:has() predicates) and assert the STATE marker, not the surface.
dom-snapshot reuses ONE page across blocks, so drive steps must be idempotent. Bare toggle clicks made block 1 open the sidebar and block 2 close it: 1/8 captured in batch vs 1/1 in isolation.
